sources.title: UW Extension: Pothos — Susan Mahr, revised Bruce Spangenberg
Iowa State Extension: Stem-tip cuttings — Aaron Steil

claims.text: UW Extension describes rooting pothos vines in water or vermiculite, taking approximately three to four weeks under warm conditions.

Iowa State lists pothos among houseplants propagated by stem-tip cuttings: prepare a three-to-six-inch stem with at least two nodes and remove lower leaves. For water rooting, change water once or twice weekly, keep developing roots submerged and pot around one-inch root length. Water-rooted cuttings may show stress after transfer to soil.

candidates.name: Root pothos cuttings in water
candidates.reason: Prepare and maintain a small water-rooting attempt; record root development and survival after transfer to potting mix. Use root development rather than calendar age alone to choose transfer timing.
limitations: Rooting time depends on indoor conditions, cutting health and cultivar. The general houseplant preparation guidance includes pothos; it is not a measured success rate.
Primary-source guidance acquired by the host agent after a peer identified a retrieval gap. No consumer trial, success rate or human usefulness has been established.
